visible_difference: Water and ledge marks change from stroked to fill-only. Today six thin stroked rain rings are clipped by the channel edge into moving arc fragments. The ledge slab carries a 3 px outline and a hard 9 px dark undercut band that reads as a line along its edge. In shot 1 a 32 plan px sliver of that slab pokes in at the upper-left frame edge. The replacement draws rain as three large soft filled discs that fade to transparent, gives the slab no outline and no band so it reads by its own pale fill on brown water, and moves the near camera so the slab is wholly out of shot 1. Nothing short, thin or edge-cut remains in the water or on the ledge.

2. Sources of the flagged marks, read in code.

(a) The six stroked rain rings (CreekPlan 'rain-rings'): circle strokes 2 px wide, #EEE7D8, opacity up to .28, radius 30 to 80, cycling at 1.3/s and clipped to the water path. Where a ring crosses the channel edge, or its fade cuts it, it shows as moving arc fragments. In shot 1 (the NEAR camera) the ring at (620, 690) lands near screen (380, 424), upper-left, and the ring at (900, 700) near (828, 440). In shot 2 (the CARRY camera) the rings at (620, 690), (330, 1060), (180, 700) and the edge rings at (900, 700) and (90, 900) land in or at the frame. These match the 'short curved strokes' at 15.2 and 15.6 s and the moving dash and slanted mark.

(b) The slab. Its outline is a 3 px #AFA48C stroke. Its undercut is a closed smoothPath of [ledgeWater + 9, ledgeBank] in #3E2F20 at .55, which shows as a hard dark band about 9 px wide (about 13 screen px in shot 2) along the slab's water edge. Its corners can overshoot past the slab ends, because it lacks the slab's own end points [la-7] and [lb+6]. Together these are the 'thin line at the ledge slab edge' at 16.2 to 17.4 s.

(c) NOT in the plan: in shot 1 the slab's right end, at plan x about 408 to 414 (with undercut overshoot possibly to about 418), lies inside CREEK_PLAN_NEAR's left edge at plan x 382.5 (f [720, 1025], s 1.6). That leaves a sliver about 32 plan px wide (about 51 screen px) at screen x 0 to about 51, y about 322 to 461: an edge-cut stub with an outline and a dark band, exactly the '14.4 s upper-left tick and dash'. It is static, so it is present throughout shot 1.
(d) Checked and not sources:
- the three stripes: ends off frame, gradient pulse only;
- the bank foam lines along T and B: pale, continuous past both frame edges; the 6·sin(.047x) wiggle makes a wavy line, not short marks;
- the stone shelf outline: long lines along the grass edge, off the water;
- the crown shadow ellipses: soft fills; the crown at (230, 560) is off shot 1 and clear in shot 2;
- the mottling blobs: soft fills;
- the collar: filled ellipses only;
- the bank-flood ellipses: fills.

(e) Possible minor contributor: the wake fades in with opacity = lift, from about 15.24 s. Around 15.4 to 15.7 s, the faint thin top strand (6 px at .65 × lift), partly hidden by the car, can read as a short curved stroke. Optional fix in RobotaxiFilm.tsx: set the wake opacity to smooth(clamp(lift × 2.5)), so it reaches full strength by lift about .4 and is never a faint fragment. The phone review confirmed the curved wake as a cue, so this is optional.

(f) Not water marks but on the car: the four dark tyre rects (76 × 22 car units, #17191C) stick out about 14 units past the TOP_BODY sides. They are on the car, not in the creek, and none of the flagged marks was on the car. Leave them.
